domain_restrictions: a, b, and r are integers
I is finite because it is the interval of integers from a+1 to b
R is graded by assigning degree s to x_s
each f_s is homogeneous in R
the family f_s indexed by I is ordered by increasing s
that ordered family is a regular sequence
A_n refers only to the degree-n homogeneous component of A

semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: Given integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, and given a finite indexed family of homogeneous polynomials f_s in the weighted graded polynomial ring R = Q[x_s : s in I] with I = {a+1, ..., b}, deg(x_s) = s, deg(f_s) = r+s, and with the f_s forming a regular sequence in increasing index order, the quotient algebra A = R divided by the ideal generated by the f_s is finite-dimensional over Q. Its Hilbert series is exactly the product over s from a+1 to b of (1 minus q to the power r+s) divided by (1 minus q to the power s). Consequently, for every nonnegative integer j, the coefficient of q to the j in that product equals dim_Q of A_j and is a nonnegative integer.
quantifier_order: Choose integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0.
Define I as the finite set of integers from a+1 to b.
Form the graded polynomial ring R over the rational numbers with variables x_s for s in I, where x_s has degree s.
For every s in I, choose a homogeneous polynomial f_s in R of degree r+s.
Require that the family (f_s) ordered by increasing s is a regular sequence.
Define A as the quotient of R by the ideal generated by all f_s.
For every nonnegative integer n, let A_n be the degree-n component of A.
Conclude that A is finite-dimensional over Q and that its Hilbert series equals the stated product.
For every nonnegative integer j, the coefficient of degree j in the product equals dim_Q A_j and is a nonnegative integer.

witness_dependencies: The family f_s is part of the input data; there is no separate existential choice of a new witness in the conclusion.
The algebra A depends on the entire family (f_s) at once, not on individual j-dependent witnesses.
For each j, the coefficient equality uses the same fixed algebra A and the same fixed Hilbert series formula.
No hidden dependence on n or j appears in the construction of A; only the graded piece A_n varies with n.

statement_nl:
Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}, let R := Q[x_s : s in I] be graded by deg(x_s) = s, and let (f_s)_{s in I} be a family of homogeneous polynomials in R such that deg(f_s) = r+s for every s in I and the ordered list by increasing s is a regular sequence. Put A := R / (f_s : s in I), and let A_n denote the degree-n homogeneous component of A. Then A is a finite-dimensional graded Q-algebra and its Hilbert series is
Hilb_A(q) = sum_{n >= 0} (dim_Q A_n) q^n = product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)).
In particular, for every integer j >= 0, the coefficient [q^j] product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) equals dim_Q A_j and is a nonnegative integer.
